title: general-verify task contract
description: The shortest possible statement of what must become true, written BEFORE the code, in a form a machine can check afterwards. Not a design document and not a ticket. Everything in this file is inside the canonical hash.

task.description: Unique task id. Red proofs, run directories and trace lines all key off this.

description.description: What must become true, in language the person who asked for it would recognise.

tier.description: How much ceremony this task warrants. quick = one person, no subagents. standard = builder + critic. full = proposer + qa first. Matching the tier to the stakes is the first real decision.

clauses.description: One requirement each. Every clause must have a case mapped to it, or it is agreed but unproven.

text.description: One requirement. A clause with 'and' in it usually wants to be two, and will otherwise be half-delivered and still marked green.

observable_by.description: How a machine could tell this clause was met. If you cannot answer, it is a wish rather than a requirement: sharpen it until you can, or move it to open_questions.

open_flag.description: An unresolved objection carried forward visibly rather than silently dropped.

units.description: The pieces of work this task splits into. Each needs at least one probe case.

surface.description: The file or module this unit lives in.

cases.description: The behaviours that must be tested. Each becomes a test, and each must be observed failing before it passes.

probe.description: An off-happy-path case: the empty input, the boundary, the hostile value, the failure path. At least one per unit - a unit with none has only tested the demo.

test_name.description: Pin the mapping to a specific test name. Only needed when the test name differs enough from the case id that matching by normalised containment would miss it.

guard.description: A regression guard: behaviour that already held and must keep holding. No red proof is expected, because by construction it was never red. Guards are counted separately from proven cases and are never counted as proofs, so they cannot be used to stand in for the ones genuinely missing.

gate.description: Override the resolved gate for this task specifically. Rarely needed - the project-level config is the usual place.

non_goals.description: Explicitly out of scope. Writing these down is what stops scope drift from being discovered at review time.
